column8:
.. code-block:: text

    Only the parameter ``molopt`` requires detailed explanation in this tool.

    After running this tool the coefficient of the contracted atomic orbitals
    are  arbitrary because all the original  wave function (in ``fort.10_in``)
    is rewritten (in ``fort.10_new``)  in terms of molecular orbitals defined
    in the original primitive basis (e.g. all independent atomic gaussian basis
    defining the original ``fort.10_in``).

    if molopt>= 2  then the coefficients of the contracted atomic
    orbitals will no longer be optimizable in a subsequent minimization.
    Otherwise all contracted atomic orbitals will be optimized with
    the corresponding option molopt=1 in datasminmol.input
    or molopt=0 (default) in datasmin.input

    By using abs(molopt)>=2 this subroutine initialize the coefficients
    of the contracted atomic orbitals,using dmrg (the system
    has to represent at best the universe) to evaluate
    the best atomic contracted orbitals (the system) that can be connected
    to the full AGP matrix squared  (the universe now written in terms
    of molecular orbitals). See the DMRG paper by S.R. White PRB 48, 10345 (1993).
    The algorithm is: be f(r1,r) the AGP obtained by restricting r1 to all
    atomic orbitals of given type (s,p,d) acting on a given atom.
    The density matrix is DMRG(r1,r2)=int_(r' \in universe)  f(r1,r') f(r2,r').
    The best atomic orbitals are the eigenvector of the density matrix
    with highest eigenvalue.

Occupations are read from standard input (see below); the number of occupations read is chosen by the parameter ``nelocc`` (``neloccdo`` for down spin electrons) which must be specified in input. In this case we have ``occupations(1:nelocc) = 2`` for LDA; ``occupations(1:nelocc) = 1`` && ``occupationdo(1:neloccdo) = 1`` for LSDA.
- ``optocc = 1``: Use a smeared Fermi distribution with a spread given by the parameter ``epsshell`` (see below). In this case:  :math:`occupations(i) = \exp{ \frac{eig(i)-ef}{epsshell}+1}` where the Fermi energy :math:`ef` is determined by the constraint, sum(occupations(1:bands)) = no. of electrons via bisection method . For LSDA (``|typedft| = 4, 5``) two Fermi distributions are introduced for up and down electrons. In the case of k-points sampling, the Fermi energy is determined by averaging over :math:`ef` computed for each k-point.

   - ``itestr4 = -9, -5`` (VMC-opt) Same as -4, -8, respectively, but using Stochastic reconfiguration (SR) wavefunction optimization method.

   - ``itestr4 = -29, -25`` (LRDMC-opt) Same as -9, -5, respectively, but the derivatives are computed using LRDMC.

.. code-block:: text

    parcutg (integer)  (default =1  a much better  choice so far tested for LRDMC,
     larger pacrutg should correspond to even better choices but still to be tested).

    parcutg=0  vpotr=vpota.

    It is well defined only when the FN approximation
    is employed otherwise the effective potential V^a is unbounded
    from below and the lattice regularization is ill defined.
    Therefore do not use parcutg=0 for sampling the sign.
    The exact energy will be -infty for any a>0.

    abs(parcutg)=1  vpotr=max(vpotc,vpota,-costtmu)

    only when the
    wavefunction changes by displacing one electron by means
    of the shorter lattice space of length a (alat).
    Otherwise vpotr=vpota.
    The error is always order a^2 within LRDMC.
    costtmu= sum_neighbor_lrdmc  1/a_mu^2
    Thus the ground state energy of H^a is bounded from below.
    Otherwise it is not guaranteed.

    abs(parcutg)=2  vpotr=max(vpotcreg,vpota)

    only when the wavefunction changes by displacing one electron by means
    of the shorter lattice space of length a (alat).
    Otherwise vpotr=vpota.
    vpotcreg = Coulomb potential with the electron-ion
    contribution regularized with  minimum el-ion distance r:
    r--> Max( r, alat ) if Z_sing>0.
    Z_sing is the singular part of the total Coulomb and
    local part of the pseudo diverging as -Z_sing/r.
    In particular when the local part of the pseudo cancels
    the Coulomb singularity Z_sing=0 and :math:`|parcutg| = 2` is equivalent
    to :math:`|parcutg| = 1`.
    The error is always order a^2 within LRDMC.
    Thus the ground state energy of H^a is bounded from below.
    Otherwise it is not guaranteed.


    parcutg<0

    Same as abs(parcutg), but choose a linear approximation in
    time  for time integrated averages and weight updates.
    This should reduce statistical fluctuation at a cost of
    a small bias that however vanishes also as alat^2
    (so it should be worth for SR or release nodes).
    Not recommended (bad performances and no control a->0).

    cutreg The cutoff acting as above when :math:`|parcutg| = 2`, can be scaled:
    alat--> alat*cutreg (Default cutreg=1).
    i.e. the minimum e-i distance is Max( r, cutreg x alat )

- description(98wavefunctionoptimization):

  - tpar: Acceleration parameter (i.e., learning rate.)

  .. code-block:: text

    tpar
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^

    For example, in the stochastic reconfiguration (SR) method, the variational parameters
    are updated as:

    .. math::

        {\alpha _k} \to {\alpha _k} + \Delta  \cdot {\left( {{{{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S'}}}}^{ - 1}}{\mathbf{f}}} \right)_k},


    where :math:`\Delta` is ``tpar``, :math:`{\mathbf{f}}` is the general force vector, and :math:`{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S'}}}` is
    the variance-covariance matrix which is stochastically evaluated by means of :math:`M` configuration samples :math:`{\mathbf{x}} = \left\{ {{{\mathbf{x}}_1},{{\mathbf{x}}_2}, \ldots {{\mathbf{x}}_M}} \right\}`:

``parr`` a hyper parameter  :math:`\varepsilon` for the regularization of the preconditioning matrix (i.e., ill-conditioned).  See the equation (130) of the review_ paper.

- description(98wavefunctionoptimization):

  - parr: Regularization (c.f., LASSO)

  .. code-block:: text

    parr
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^

    The straightforward implementation of the SR method is not stable mainly because the statistical noise sometimes makes the matrix :math:`{\boldsymbol{\mathcal{S}}}` ill-conditioned,
    which deteriorates the efficiency of the optimization method. Therefore, in practice, the diagonal elements of the  preconditioning matrix :math:`{\mathcal{S}}` are shifted by a small positive parameter (:math:`\varepsilon`) as:

    .. math::

        {s'_{i,i}} = {s_{i.i}}(1 + \varepsilon ),

    where :math:`\varepsilon` = ``parr`` in TurboRVB.

    This modification improves the efficiency of the optimization by  several orders of magnitude.

- description(DFT):

This integer specifies the type of k-points which will be chosen in the calculation.

   - ``kp_type = 0``: Do not perform any k-points sampling and use the phase specified in the ``fort.10`` as the unique k-point.

   - ``kp_type = 1``: Use the Monkhorst-Pack algorithm to generate equally-spaced k-points in the first Brillouin zone. The size of the grid in the three Cartesian directions is determined by the integers ``nk1, nk2, nk3``. Note that ``nk1`` must be set to a value > 0. If ``nk2, nk3`` are not set, then they are taken to be equal to ``nk1``. Also, if skip_equivalence (see below) is set to ``.false.`` the number of k-points might be reduced.
                   In this case, run the tool ``find_kpoints.x`` with the desired input in order to know how many processors must be allocated.

   - ``kp_type = 2``: When this is used, k-points are set by the user and their number is specified by the integer ``nk1``. In this case, the section **KPOINTS** is needed (see below).

   - ``kp_type = 3``: Generates k-points path along high-symmetry lines in the first Brillouin zone. The initial and final points of these segments are specified in the section **KPOINTS** (see below). The number of extremal points is specified by the integer ``nk1`` and the number of points in each segment is specified by the integer ``nk2``.

   - ``kp_type = 4``: Generate k-points randomly within the first Brillouin zone. The number of k-points is specified by ``nk1``. **KPOINTS** section is not needed.
